Roger and team — thanks, we've completed the technical responses in the attached sheet and summarized the main points below. Markus will follow up with contractual language.

Summary of Redwood hosted API residency & retention (concise):

1) Data residency and region controls
- Default: customer request data (API inputs) and derived outputs are stored in the region selected at account creation (US-EAST, US-WEST, EU-WEST, APAC-1).
- Replication: cross-region replication is not enabled by default. Multi-region replication is only performed when explicitly configured by the customer (for DR or latency reasons).
- Region pinning: customers can request hard region pinning via our onboarding form or addendum; we will prevent cross-region backups unless the addendum is executed.

2) Retention windows (hosted API default settings)
- Request logs (metadata for debugging & billing): 30 days by default; can be shortened to contractually-agreed shorter windows.
- Raw model inputs/outputs: 30 days by default for hosted API; customers can opt into longer retention for debugging or analytics use cases under contract.
- Derived artifacts (embeddings/vector indexes): retained 90 days by default; can be configured shorter via account settings or contract.
- KV/prefix caches and in-memory caches: TTLs range 0-7 days depending on workload and optimization; not persisted to long-term storage by default.

3) Deletion and purge processes
- Customer-initiated erasure: we perform a soft-delete immediately in primary stores, which prevents further access. Background purge removes data from primary stores within 72 hours in most cases.
- Backups/snapshots: backups are retained for a 90-day rolling window by default; deletion from backups is asynchronous and may take up to 90 days. We can negotiate reduced backup retention windows in contract for regulated workloads.
- Audit trail: deletion operations are logged and available in the Console audit logs; audit logs are retained for 1 year by default (can be extended under enterprise plans).

4) Cryptography and key management
- Data in transit: TLS 1.2+ enforced for all API endpoints.
- Data at rest: AES-256 encryption for stored objects.
- Customer-managed keys: supported via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault). HSM-backed keys available for Private/Dedicated deployments; hosted customers can use CMKs where required.

5) Compliance and assurances
- Redwood is SOC 2 Type II audited; we provide the SOC 2 report under NDA.
- We maintain standard incident response and data breach notification timelines as per our DPA (30 days to notify on confirmed breaches).

Questions for Cascade (items we flagged):
- Do you require backup retention < 90 days? If so, we will propose a backup retention addendum.
- Do you require immediate certificate of deletion (attestation) for every erasure request, or is a console/audit log entry sufficient? We can generate an attestation PDF when required.

Attached: completed questionnaire + short retention summary (PDF).

Best,
Soojin Lee
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

3) Geo-restriction on telemetry: We want telemetry and billing logs to remain in-region; would that be covered by the region pinning addendum or is that separate?

Roger — appreciate the clear asks. We can support the following and will incorporate into a short addendum for signature:

- Erasure SLA: Redwood will commit to a purge-from-primary SLA of 72 hours for customer-initiated erasure requests on hosted API accounts. We will provide an attestation PDF for each regulated erasure request within 5 business days of completion.
- Backup purge timeline: Redwood will document a backup purge window of up to 90 days by default; for regulated accounts we will offer a negotiated backup retention window (minimum achievable contractually is 30 days, depending on DR requirements).
- Telemetry/geofencing: Telemetry and billing logs can be region-pinned via the region pinning addendum; we'll ensure in-region storage unless you opt into cross-region processing.

Next steps:
- I will ask Legal to prepare a one-page Data Residency & Erasure addendum reflecting the SLA above and the attestation process.
- Please confirm you want the 72-hour primary purge SLA and the option to negotiate backup retention down to 30 days. If yes, I'll get the addendum into DocuSign and we can complete procurement quickly.

If it helps, here is suggested clause language you can include in vendor documentation: 

"Vendor shall, upon Customer's written request, initiate deletion of Customer Data in primary production stores and complete removal of Customer Data from primary production storage within seventy-two (72) hours. Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to remove Customer Data from backups and archived storage within ninety (90) days; if Customer requires a shorter backup retention period, the parties shall negotiate and document such retention in an addendum."

I'll kick off Legal and Ben will coordinate pricing impact (if any). Can we schedule a 30-minute call Monday to finalize?

Thanks,
